You know what? I have been disillusioned for many years now. Not only in tech or media, but humanity as a whole. Let me explain. When I was in my teens, I would watch in awe 2 shows. Start Trek : The Next Generation, and later Deep Space 9. I didn't watch any later ones, nor the original series, but in this case, it didn't matter. Those 2 were probably the most inspirational to me ever, because they showed what humankind could achieve if it aimed for greatness and continuous self improvement. People doing their things not out of necessity, but because they would strive for greater things. It didn't matter if they were exploring new galaxies (Picard), writing stories (Jake Sisko) or just cooking (Cmdr Sisko's father, can't remember the name now). It filled me with the idea, that maybe not im my lifetime, but this would be in some way humanity's future, and that this is the next cultural evolution of our species. Sure, this was just a scifi show, and it took a lot of liberties, like the idea that humanity kinda-sorta has infinite resources at it's disposal. But it's not the details that mattered, but the human condition that Picard has always sparred about with Q. Our ability to adapt, to learn from past mistakes, and the need to better ourselves, the constant pursuit of knowledge, etc.

Fast forward to today. Watching this show fills me with nothing but contempt for my species. I don't want to point fingers, there's just too many factors. But not in my wildest nightmares did I think that we can stoop so low. That instead of striving up to better ourselves, we drown those who excel. That even with this kind of technology, we seem to regress to apathy, sensationalism, tribalism, probably more -ism words. It's just too sad to think about sometimes.

Sorry for the kinda offtopic rant, but I just had to get it out of my system.
